title.narrative: Strengthening CSO¿s responses to COVID-19 pandemic and support of vulnerable youth and children in Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City

description.narrative: The overall objective of the Action: Strengthened CSOs in Vietnam effectively contribute to the Governments COVID-19 response to support the most affected children and youth. Outcome/Specific Objectives: CSOs in Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City effectively address challenges stemming from the COVID-19 pandemic and extend their support to migrant youth and children, especially gender-vulnerable migrants (e.g., girls, non-binary), so that they can access decent work and social protection service.The overall objective of the Action: Strengthened CSOs in Vietnam effectively contribute to the Governments COVID-19 response to support the most affected children and youth. Outcome/Specific Objectives: CSOs in Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City effectively address challenges stemming from the COVID-19 pandemic and extend their support to migrant youth and children, especially gender-vulnerable migrants (e.g., girls, non-binary), so that they can access decent work and social protection services Estimated outputs: Output 1: At least 2 CSOs in Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh city have the capacity to address challenges stemming from COVID-19 pandemic and are skilled to support migrant children and youth response to COVID-19 Output 2: Migrant children and youth, especially gender vulnerable young people, are able to access quality protection services through the support of CSOs Output 3: Migrant youth, especially gender vulnerable young people, are equipped with necessary soft and entrepreneurship skills through support from local CSOs and are able to maintain sustainable livelihood opportunities and increase their resilience. Output 4. : Active CSOs, their networks and migrant youth and children are more engaged in government decision making during a crisis. Target groups: -At least 600 migrant children and youth (300 children and 300 youth), especially gender vulnerable youth, aged 6 to 25. This group includes, but not limited to, migrant youth who work in factories in industrial zones, informal sectors like street vendors, as well as migrant children who followed their parents that suffered income loss from economic shocks. -Two local CSOs: The CSOs Ho Chi Minh City Children Welfare Association (HCWA) and the Centre of Help for Indigenous value promotion and Sustainable Environment (CHIASE). -Staff of local authorities: Department of Children, Ministry of Labour, Invalids and Social Affairs (MOLISA) and Ho Chi Minh Department of Labour, Invalids and Social Affairs (DOLISA) Final beneficiaries: 15,000 Parents, families, communities, migrant children and youth; at least 150 CSOs;
